$comment: The work queue for this repository. `verification` is the only path out of `active`, and the harness runs it — never the agent. CI re-runs every passing claim, so editing `state` by hand is detected rather than trusted.

items.behavior: A documentation claim whose evidence disappeared fails the gate, naming the document, the line and the reason, while an example that documents the marker syntax is left alone.
items.evidence: # pass 10 | # fail 0 | # cancelled 0 | # skipped 0 | # todo 0 | # duration_ms 121.900818

items.behavior: The track index cannot point at a handoff that no longer exists, a track without a status fails, and a checked box in a live lane names a check that resolves.
items.evidence: # pass 13 | # fail 0 | # cancelled 0 | # skipped 0 | # todo 0 | # duration_ms 120.035956

items.behavior: An item whose state was edited by hand is caught, because every passing claim is re-run rather than believed, and an item whose success cannot be decided may not be started at all.
items.evidence: # pass 16 | # fail 0 | # cancelled 0 | # skipped 0 | # todo 0 | # duration_ms 122.173915

items.behavior: An agent commit touching the files that define success fails while the same change by a human passes, and a document routing a reader outside the repository fails the cold-start check.
items.evidence: # pass 9 | # fail 0 | # cancelled 0 | # skipped 0 | # todo 0 | # duration_ms 115.167635

items.behavior: The command line reads configuration, finds the documents, scaffolds a working harness with init, and exits non-zero on a broken claim — proven against real repositories on disk rather than mocks.
items.evidence: # pass 6 | # fail 0 | # cancelled 0 | # skipped 0 | # todo 0 | # duration_ms 676.733452

items.behavior: This repository passes every check it defines, so the standard is demonstrated by its own repository rather than only described in it.
items.evidence: ok    proof markers  25 proof marker(s) across 18 document(s) all resolve |   ok    work tracks    2 live track(s) in specs/TRACKS.md resolve and carry a status |   ok    task gate      checked boxes in 1 live task list(s) name a passing check |   ok    queue          queue invariants hold (nested run: invariants only) | harness: every configured check passes.

items.behavior: Debris a build compiles happily — a leftover marker, a stale progress file, an instruction file that grew into a manual — fails a check scoped to what the session actually changed.
items.evidence: # pass 9 | # fail 0 | # cancelled 0 | # skipped 0 | # todo 0 | # duration_ms 115.183574
items.notes: Lectures 12 and 04 of Learn Harness Engineering. Added on explicit human instruction to use the course's concepts where they fit.

items.behavior: A repository adopting the tool gets a configuration written from what it already has — its command runner, source directories, migrations and CI — whose first run is green, with everything left off reported and explained.
items.evidence: # pass 12 | # fail 0 | # cancelled 0 | # skipped 0 | # todo 0 | # duration_ms 617.979927
items.notes: The failure this removes: a template configuration whose first run fails on settings nobody chose, which is how adoption stalls.

items.behavior: A repository gets the fast gates on every commit with one command, through a hook checked into the repository, and can ask whether git is actually using it rather than assuming a file that exists is a file that runs.
items.evidence: # pass 8 | # fail 0 | # cancelled 0 | # skipped 0 | # todo 0 | # duration_ms 80.222249
items.notes: Prompted by the question 'are hooks wired up at all' — which found a hook in the sibling repository still calling a script this migration had deleted.

items.behavior: A session receives the harness state at startup — live tracks, the head of each handoff, what is in flight, what is and is not enforced — instead of being trusted to go and read it.
items.evidence: # pass 12 | # fail 0 | # cancelled 0 | # skipped 0 | # todo 0 | # duration_ms 84.545629
items.notes: Asked whether the agent-side hooks were wired up: they were not, except one hand-written script in one repository that needed jq.
